description: Controlled EvidenceCard mutations grounded in archived real paper text. Labels are agent proposals, not human gold labels.

tf_tgn.title: Retrofitting Temporal Graph Neural Networks with Transformer
tf_tgn.quote: In this paper, we propose TF-TGN, which uses Transformer decoder as the backbone model for TGNN to enjoy Transformer's codebase for efficient training.

tncn.title: Efficient Neural Common Neighbor for Temporal Graph Link Prediction
tncn.quote: We propose TNCN for temporal graph link prediction, which employs a temporal common neighbor extractor combined with a memory-based node representation learning module.

cases.claim: Use Transformer decoders for temporal graph neural networks.
cases.contribution: TF-TGN uses a Transformer decoder as its TGNN backbone for efficient training.
overlaps: Uses a Transformer decoder for temporal graph neural networks.
cases.rationale: Quote explicitly states the backbone and application. No claim of global novelty or measured speed.

cases.claim: Combine temporal common neighbors with memory-based node representations for link prediction.
cases.contribution: TNCN combines a temporal common neighbor extractor and memory-based node representations for temporal link prediction.
cases.rationale: Direct paraphrase of the archived conclusion; no performance extrapolation.

cases.claim: Use Transformer decoders for temporal graph neural networks.
cases.contribution: The abstract reports a Transformer decoder backbone for TGNN; this card makes no claim about full-text experiments or superiority.
cases.rationale: An abstract can support a bounded architecture claim without full-text access.

cases.claim: Use Transformer decoders for temporal graph neural networks.
cases.contribution: TF-TGN explicitly avoids Transformer decoders and uses only an LSTM backbone.
cases.rationale: The asserted backbone directly contradicts the quoted Transformer decoder backbone.

cases.claim: Combine temporal common neighbors with memory-based node representations for link prediction.
cases.contribution: TNCN has no memory-based node representation module.
cases.rationale: Quote explicitly includes a memory-based module.

cases.claim: A chemical catalyst increases hydrogen production yield.
cases.contribution: TF-TGN uses a Transformer decoder backbone for temporal graph neural networks.
overlaps: This provides direct evidence for increased catalytic hydrogen yield.
cases.rationale: A temporal graph architecture claim has no semantic support for catalytic yield, despite matching task IDs and high input relevance.

cases.claim: Use Transformer decoders for temporal graph neural networks.
cases.contribution: TF-TGN uses a Transformer decoder backbone.
differences: Unlike the target, TF-TGN does not use any Transformer decoder.
cases.rationale: Overlap and difference explicitly contradict each other and the quote.

cases.contribution: TF-TGN uses a Transformer decoder and improves training speed by exactly 2.20 times in every dataset.
cases.rationale: Architecture is supported, but the supplied quote contains no measurements. Request experiment evidence rather than infer falsehood from absence.

cases.claim: Combine temporal common neighbors with memory-based node representations for link prediction.
cases.contribution: TNCN combines common neighbors with memory-based representations.
differences: TNCN never uses an RNN anywhere in its implementation.
cases.rationale: The quote does not identify the memory update architecture. Missing evidence cannot establish absence of RNNs.

cases.claim: Use Transformer decoders for temporal graph neural networks.
cases.contribution: The full text proves that this architecture is universally optimal on every possible temporal graph.
cases.rationale: Only an abstract architecture sentence is supplied, no theorem. The universal claim is unsupported; do not assert it has been disproved.

cases.claim: Use Transformer decoders for temporal graph neural networks.
